newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on central bank moves.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on central bank moves.

text.p: Investor caution over central bank moves to tighten liquidity erased early-session gains on Tuesday to break the Taiwan stock market's four-day rise, sending the index to a slightly lower close, brokers said.
The central bank issued T$11 billion negotiable certificates of deposit after the market's close on Monday to mop up excess money, a move widely seen as aiming to cool the red-hot bourse.
The index spiked to a seven-year intraday high of 9,371.50 early on Tuesday before turning soft to close at 9,305.27, a loss of 17.57 points or 0.19 percent from Monday's close.
Turnover was heavy at T$175.8 billion.
"The correction was expected, partly reflecting caution over the central bank move and partly due to resistance at 9,400-9,600," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
"Investors fear that the central bank might take further moves to cool down the stock market, so many are taking profits first," Lee said.
Financials fell most, followed by chemicals, constructions and plastics.
Recent bellwether electronics struggled with profit-takers through the session but, showing its contrarian spirit, ended with a 0.95 percent gain to defy the market downturn.
